term: can fail to be (Met. IX.8) / can be otherwise (Met. XII.7)
resolution: Both render ἐνδέχεται with a contrary state, and the Lambda.7 route to pure act passes from one to the other, so the passage is made explicit. CanFailToBe (IX.8, 1050b8-15; In Metaph. IX, lect. 9 n. 2-4) is read in the two-way sense of the potency of the contradictory: what is in potency to r is able to be r and able not to be r. CanBeOtherwise (XII.7, 1072b4-8; In Metaph. XII, lect. 7 n. 12-13) is the ability to be other than one is in r. The case keeps two primitives. STMT-EVERY-POTENCY-IS-OF-CONTRADICTION uses only CanFailToBe; STMT-SOME-UNMOVED-MOVER-CANNOT-BE-OTHERWISE and STMT-EVERY-UNMOVED-MOVER-CANNOT-BE-OTHERWISE use only CanBeOtherwise. The step between them is the explicit, unattributed bridge STMT-WHAT-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-CAN-BE-OTHERWISE, which holds in the two-way sense and fails if 'can fail to be r' is read as the bare possibility of not being r (an unchangeable being that is not r would have it). No argument identifies the two predicates silently. In Metaph. XII, lect. 7 n. 13-15 does not supply the bridge: it glosses the necessary as what cannot not be (said of the first motion) and as what cannot be otherwise (absolute necessity), and n. 15 denies that the first motion's necessity is of the second kind.
